sources.title: Korasick et al. (2014), Molecular basis for AUXIN RESPONSE FACTOR protein interaction and the control of auxin response repression

findings.location: helix, lines 23-30; consumers auxinProcess.js, plantDefenseProcess.js and root-owned photosynthesisProcess.js
findings.evidence: The actual TubeGeometry path is [r*cos(theta), y, +r*sin(theta)]. Its consecutive tangent triple products are negative (first: -4.09006684e-6 for FLS2 TM), whereas downloaded 2P1Q chain A HELIX 1 class-1 CA points give +45.2551, +43.5270, +40.0061. Proper quaternion rotations preserve the sign. All consumers use positive scales.
findings.whyWrong: This constructs left-handed protein alpha-helix cartoons throughout both processes, opposite the deposited ordinary right-handed alpha helices. The error also propagates through domain and lrr decorative helices and root photosynthesis.
findings.fix: Reverse the transverse sine orientation in the owned helix helper, preserving radius, turn count, center, endpoints and all call-site transforms. Root will cross-reference this issue for photosynthesis.
findings.verification: Compare signed torsion of generated path to class-1 deposited CA helices; assert positive handedness under representative non-axis-aligned calls and positive scales, unchanged endpoint locations/radius/axial extent, and rerun owned scientific regression.

findings.location: ARF PB1 at lines 177-182; Aux/IAA body at 202-210; update position lines 429-437
findings.evidence: At p=0, and for the entire low-auxin branch, ARF PB1 and the Aux/IAA compact body have identical world centers [-1.44,-1.29,0.02]. Their scales are [0.47,0.45,0.5] and [0.58,0.54,0.6]. All 1700 actual sampled PB1 lobe vertices lie inside one of the rendered Aux/IAA ellipsoid lobes.
findings.whyWrong: The smaller ARF domain is swallowed by the repressor volume rather than meeting it at a protein-protein interface; this hides the molecular identities exactly where repression is introduced.
findings.fix: Place the free Aux/IAA body at a distinct touching PB1 surface and interpolate to the existing experimental TIR1 docking pose; preserve the exact common 2P1Q bound transform and the later proteasome trajectory.
findings.verification: Assert distinct initial centers, small actual surface contact gap, and bounded shallow intersection rather than whole-domain containment at p=0 and all low-auxin states; check departing intermediate states and existing 2P1Q contact test.

findings.location: unfoldedSubstrate creation lines 316-326 and update lines 471-473
findings.evidence: At p=0.63588264 (loss=0.02), a prebuilt substrate thread switches from invisible to visible at world length 1.167386. At p=0.69411736 (loss=0.98), it switches off while still 0.951505 long. Only 20% y scaling is applied, so the entire strand pops rather than being fed through the proteasome. Samples +/-1e-7 confirm finite visible-size jumps, not a small terminal visibility threshold.
findings.whyWrong: The dominant degradation strand appears and disappears at near full size during continuous playback, weakening the intended causal continuity from Aux/IAA to unfolded substrate and fragments.
findings.fix: Use an allocation-free progressively revealed/consumed prebuilt thread with an end anchored to the substrate/entry path; make end visibility changes occur only after represented length or opacity tends to zero while preserving ubiquitin recycling and peptide outputs.
findings.verification: Sample immediately around both thresholds and throughout degradation; visible length or opacity must approach zero at appearance/disappearance, and substrate-to-thread attachment must remain continuous. Keep deterministic irregular seeks and stable geometry/material/node inventories.

findings: 20261004-plantSignals-03: near-full-length substrate thread visibility jumps; no rendered acceptance yet.
limits: Polypeptide shape and folding/unfolding motions are schematic, not atomistic trajectories.

sources.title: 4MN8 and Sun et al. (2013), Structural basis for flg22-induced activation of the Arabidopsis FLS2-BAK1 immune complex
sources.supports: Experimental FLS2/BAK1 ectodomain/flg22 complex. flg22 lies along the FLS2 inner surface; BAK1 contacts FLS2 and the flg22 C terminus. Supports distinct interacting ectodomains rather than overlapping solids.

sources.title: Li et al. (2014), The FLS2-associated kinase BIK1 directly phosphorylates the NADPH oxidase RbohD to control plant immunity
sources.supports: Abstract: BIK1 is part of the FLS2 complex, directly phosphorylates RbohD at specific sites and promotes induced ROS; also regulates calcium influx. Supports this branch and its stated omission of cooperating inputs.

findings.location: FLS2/BAK1 ectodomain construction lines 159-217 and BAK1 trajectory lines 411-414
findings.evidence: For p>=0.48 BAK1 is at [-3.3,0,0]. A common world z-ray at x=-3.02,y=0.71 crosses FLS2 main closed solid over [-0.224632,0.224632] and BAK1 main closed solid over [-0.155000,0.195000]. Thus 0.350000 scene units of BAK1 solid are inside FLS2, spanning its entire local depth. Restricting the test to the two main ExtrudeGeometry meshes reproduces it; it is not AABB or decorative-helix evidence. Overlap is already 0.253126 at p=0.45.
findings.whyWrong: FLS2 and BAK1 should meet at an exposed ligand-dependent interface. The current two ectodomains pass into and occupy the same solid volume, despite a passing regression that tests only their cytosolic kinases.
findings.fix: Adjust the BAK1 approach/final pose and any necessary cytosolic flexible tether transforms so the ectodomains contact without bulk overlap and BAK1 still touches the FLS2-bound peptide. Retain membrane containment and existing kinase/BIK1 contacts.
findings.verification: Measure actual triangle-surface contact and solid intersection of main ectodomains over approach and docked frames; separately assert FLS2-flg22 and BAK1-flg22 contact, membrane footprint/refill, and kinase/BIK1/RBOHD contact.

findings.evidence: Each marker uses t=(p*2.6+i/5)%1 and remains visible whenever output>0.03. At active wrap samples p +/-1e-7 the same visible 0.033-radius sphere jumps 1.239999 scene units from y~0.54 to y~-0.7. Multiple wraps occur during the ROS stage; no size/opacity envelope conceals the reset.
findings.whyWrong: The visible electron teleport spans almost 19 marker diameters across the membrane. This breaks smooth directional flow even though each within-cycle path runs from cytosol toward apoplast.
findings.fix: Keep one-way illustrative flow but fade or smoothly shrink markers at both ends and only reset while invisible; base onset on output so initial flow also enters smoothly. Do not reinterpret marker count as reaction stoichiometry.
findings.verification: At all analytical wrap times and onset, compare position weighted by visible size/opacity; any full reset must occur at zero visible weight. Verify absent condition, finite buffers and repeated seeks.
